evals.name: postgres-dev
evals.prompt: Start Postgres 16 for local development with Apple's container tool. The data must survive restarts and I want to connect from my Mac with psql.
evals.expected_output: A detached postgres container with a named volume and a published port, no interactive flags, and the cleanup commands.
assertions: Uses `container run` with `-d`, not `docker`
Persists data with a named volume (`-v <name>:/var/lib/postgresql/data`), not an anonymous one
Publishes the port with `-p 5432:5432`
Does not pass `-it` to a command it runs itself
Names the container with the `agent-` prefix or gives the user an explicit name
Shows how to stop and remove the container and the volume

evals.name: machine-systemd
evals.prompt: I want a persistent Ubuntu environment on my M3 Mac where my projects are visible and I can run services with systemctl. Set it up with Apple container.
evals.expected_output: A container machine from a systemd-enabled image, with the home-mount risk stated and resources set.
assertions: Chooses `container machine create`, not `container run`
Says a bare image lacks systemd and builds or names an image with `/sbin/init` and systemd
States that the Mac home is mounted read-write with passwordless sudo by default, or creates it with `--home-mount ro`
Sets `--memory` or notes the default is half of host RAM
Runs commands with `container machine run -n <name> <cmd>`, not an interactive shell

evals.name: multiarch-push
evals.prompt: Build my Node app's image for both Apple silicon and x86-64 servers and push it to registry.example.com/team/app:1.0 with Apple container.
evals.expected_output: A two-arch build, registry login and image push using container commands only.
assertions: Builds with `container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64`
Logs in with `container registry login registry.example.com`
Pushes with `container image push`
Does not use `docker buildx` or any `docker` command

evals.name: nginx-unreachable-macos15
evals.prompt: I ran `container run -d nginx` on macOS 15. http://localhost does not load and another container cannot curl it. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: No published port, and macOS 15 isolates containers from each other.
assertions: Explains that no port was published and gives `-p 8080:80`
States that on macOS 15 containers cannot reach each other and this needs macOS 26
Does not suggest `container network create` as a fix on macOS 15

evals.name: bare-hostname-custom-network
evals.prompt: On macOS 26 I created a network with `container network create app` and started `api` and `db` on it. From api, `ping db` fails. Why?
evals.expected_output: Bare-hostname lookup on custom networks is not implemented yet; use the IP or a domain-qualified name on default.
assertions: States that lookup by bare hostname on a custom network does not work yet
Suggests the container's IP from `container inspect` or `container ls`
Does not claim a Compose-style service discovery flag exists

evals.name: anonymous-volume-leak
evals.prompt: Every time I run `container run --rm -v /data myimage` a volume is left behind. How do I find and remove them?
evals.expected_output: Anonymous volumes survive --rm; find them by the anonymous label, not by name.
assertions: States that `--rm` does not remove anonymous volumes
Finds them by the `com.apple.container.resource.anonymous` label, not by grepping for `anon`
Recommends a named volume to avoid the leak
Asks before or warns about `container volume prune` removing every unreferenced volume

evals.name: untrusted-code-sandbox
evals.prompt: I have a Python script from a stranger on the internet. Run it safely with Apple container on macOS 26 and show me its output.
evals.expected_output: A plain container with no ssh, no writable host mounts and an internal network.
assertions: Uses a plain container, not a container machine
Does not pass `--ssh`
Does not mount `$HOME`, and mounts the script read-only or copies it in
Uses a network created with `--internal` or otherwise removes internet access
Removes the container afterwards

evals.name: plain-http-registry
evals.prompt: Pulling from my local registry at 10.0.0.5:5000 fails with a TLS error. It serves plain HTTP.
evals.expected_output: Pass --scheme http.
assertions: Uses `--scheme http`
Does not claim an `auto` scheme value exists

evals.name: builder-oom
evals.prompt: `container build` of my Rust project gets killed for memory halfway through. How do I give it more?
evals.expected_output: Recreate the builder with more CPUs and memory.
assertions: States the builder VM defaults to 2 CPUs and 2 GiB
Gives `container builder stop`, `container builder delete`, then `container builder start --cpus N --memory M`

evals.name: host-service-from-container
evals.prompt: My API runs on my Mac at port 8000. How does a container reach it?
evals.expected_output: A localhost DNS domain with its Private Relay caveat.
assertions: Uses `sudo container system dns create <domain> --localhost <ip>`
Mentions that this disables Private Relay or is lost on restart
Asks before running the sudo command, or leaves it for the user to run

evals.name: cluster-local-image
evals.prompt: Spin up a local Kubernetes cluster with Apple container and run the image I just built as my-app:dev without pushing it anywhere.
evals.expected_output: A cluster with --shared-image-store, its security caveat, and kubectl with an explicit context.
assertions: Uses `container cluster create --shared-image-store`
Warns that nodes can then read every local image, including private ones
Notes that the cluster is added to `~/.kube/config`
Uses `kubectl --context <name>` rather than switching the user's current context silently

evals.name: cluster-after-system-stop
evals.prompt: I ran `container system stop` and `container system start`. Now kubectl cannot reach my container cluster. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Delete and recreate the cluster.
assertions: States the control plane does not come back after a system stop
Gives `container cluster delete` then `container cluster create` with the same name

evals.name: commit-running
evals.prompt: I installed a bunch of tools in my running container `work`. Save it as an image without stopping it.
evals.expected_output: container commit on the running container.
assertions: Uses `container commit work <image:tag>`
Does not require stopping the container first

evals.name: disk-growing
evals.prompt: Apple container is eating my disk. Free up space.
evals.expected_output: Measure, clean running containers, and ask before prunes.
assertions: Runs `container system df` first
Mentions `container clean` for running containers
Asks before `container image prune --all`, `container volume prune` or `container prune`

evals.name: install
evals.prompt: How do I install Apple's container tool?
evals.expected_output: Signed pkg from GitHub releases, then system start.
assertions: Points to the signed `.pkg` on github.com/apple/container/releases
Does not give a `brew install` command
Gives `container system start` after install
Says it needs Apple silicon and that macOS 26 is the supported version

evals.name: agent-shell-request
evals.prompt: Open a shell in an ubuntu container and tell me which version of Python it ships with.
evals.expected_output: A non-interactive one-off run, since the agent has no TTY.
assertions: Runs `container run --rm ubuntu:<tag> <command>` without `-it`
Reports the version found

evals.name: clean-everything
evals.prompt: Remove all my Apple containers and images.
evals.expected_output: Lists what exists and asks before destructive bulk commands.
assertions: Lists containers and images before deleting
Asks for confirmation before `container rm --all` or `container image prune --all`

evals.name: dns-names
evals.prompt: I want to open my container `web` at http://web.test from Safari instead of an IP.
evals.expected_output: Both DNS steps with the service restart.
assertions: Sets `[dns] domain = "test"` in `~/.config/container/config.toml`
Restarts the service with `container system stop` and `container system start`
Runs or gives `sudo container system dns create test`

evals.name: machine-resize
evals.prompt: I ran `container machine set -n dev memory=16G` but `free -h` inside still shows the old amount.
evals.expected_output: Settings apply after stop and start.
assertions: States that `set` applies only after the next stop and start
Gives `container machine stop dev` then `container machine run -n dev`

evals.name: ssh-private-clone
evals.prompt: Clone my private GitHub repo inside an alpine container using my Mac's SSH keys.
evals.expected_output: --ssh, which the user asked for.
assertions: Uses `--ssh`
Does not copy private key files into the container
